records.title: Psychological inoculation improves resilience against misinformation on social media.
records.design: 7 preregistered studies: 6 RCTs (n=6464) + 1 ecologically valid field study on YouTube (n=22,632)
records.population_setting: General adult social-media users, online panels + YouTube ad viewers
records.key_finding: Five short videos inoculating against manipulation techniques (emotionally manipulative language, incoherence, false dichotomies, scapegoating, ad hominem) improved manipulation-technique recognition, boosted confidence in spotting techniques, increased discernment of trustworthy vs untrustworthy content, and improved quality of sharing decisions, across n=6464 (RCTs) and n=22,632 (field).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: Layer 0 awareness mechanism -- direct causal evidence that brief exposure to the pattern of a manipulation technique (not the specific deceptive content itself) raises subsequent independent recognition of that technique in new material. This is the closest existing PubMed-indexed evidence for the author's core claim that 'recognising the pattern once' confers resistance. Caveat: domain is media/political misinformation, not interpersonal coercive-relationship manipulation -- an analogy, not a direct transplant.

records.title: Psychological inoculation improves resilience to and reduces willingness to share vaccine misinformation.
records.design: 3 preregistered RCTs (N=2,326)
records.population_setting: General adult online participants
records.key_finding: A short game ('Bad Vaxx') exposing people to weakened doses of manipulation techniques used in vaccine misinformation significantly improved discernment of misinformation from non-misinformation, raised confidence in that discernment, and improved quality of sharing decisions.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: Layer 0 awareness mechanism -- replicates the inoculation-improves-recognition finding in a second content domain (health/vaccine claims), reinforcing generalisability of 'brief exposure to technique pattern -> improved independent recognition' as a mechanism class, though again not interpersonal-relationship coercion specifically (analogy).

records.title: Video inoculation against election misinformation across 12 EU nations.
records.design: 13 surveys / embedded experiments across 12 EU nations (N=19,735), field campaign reaching 120M+ YouTube views
records.population_setting: General population across 12 EU countries, including older adults (45+)
records.key_finding: Prebunking videos targeting scapegoating, decontextualization, and discrediting tactics improved manipulation and technique discernment (correct identification of tactics) and reduced willingness to share manipulative content, across diverse cultures and age groups, ahead of the 2024 EU elections. Effects were small but statistically significant across surveys (ds ≈ 0.08-0.38); longer (50s) videos showed more consistent improvement than shorter (20s) ones.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: Layer 0 awareness mechanism generalising across cultures/languages/age at scale (N=19,735, 12 nations) -- useful evidence that brief technique-forewarning transfers beyond WEIRD single-country samples, relevant to T-PHE's Thai population target. Still media/political-misinformation domain, not interpersonal coercion (analogy).

records.title: Good News about Bad News: Gamified Inoculation Boosts Confidence and Cognitive Immunity Against Fake News.
records.design: 2 (treatment vs control) x 2 (pre vs post) mixed design RCT, N=196; replication/extension of the 'Bad News' game study
records.population_setting: General online participants
records.key_finding: Playing the Bad News game (learning 6 common misinformation techniques) improved participants' ability to spot manipulation techniques in fake headlines relative to control, addressing prior design gaps (added control group, more test items, attitudinal-certainty measures).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: Layer 0 awareness mechanism -- independent replication strengthens the evidence base that active/gamified pattern-exposure (not passive warning) improves later recognition; relevant if T-PHE's self-check/signals tool is interactive rather than purely informational. Domain is online misinformation headlines, not interpersonal relationship coercion -- analogy only, not a direct transplant.

records.title: Technique-based inoculation against real-world misinformation.
records.design: 2 experiments, total n=2188, convenience sample via Bad News platform
records.population_setting: General online participants
records.key_finding: Technique-based inoculation (teaching the general manipulation technique rather than a specific false claim) reduced susceptibility to real-world viral misinformation that used the trained-against techniques (Cohen's d = 0.37, p < 0.001), and conferred cross-protection against misinformation using techniques not explicitly trained on, though at a substantially reduced effect size (d = 0.10, p = 0.001).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: Layer 0 awareness mechanism -- directly evidences 'cross-protection' (recognising a technique-class generalises to unencountered examples), which is the specific claim T-PHE leans on ('recognised the pattern the first time'). Domain is misinformation, not relationship coercion -- explicit analogy only.

records.title: Disentangling Item and Testing Effects in Inoculation Research on Online Misinformation: Solomon Revisited.
records.design: 2 online studies, total N=2,159, Solomon four-group-style design
records.population_setting: General online participants
records.key_finding: Methodological study interrogating whether observed inoculation effects on misinformation recognition reflect genuine learning versus item-repetition or pretest-sensitization artifacts. Finds inoculation effects are somewhat influenced by item effects but NOT by testing effects, and confirms inoculation interventions are effective at improving people's ability to spot misinformation techniques (without making people more broadly skeptical of real news) -- a reassuring result with one methodological caveat, not a refutation.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates: a methodological caution relevant to any future T-PHE evaluation design -- if T-PHE later measures 'recognition improved after Layer 0 exposure' via pre/post self-check items, this paper flags that naive pre/post designs can inflate apparent recognition gains through item effects specifically (though not through pretest-sensitization/testing effects). Useful for the evaluation-design section, not for claiming T-PHE works. Misinformation domain only -- analogy, not a direct transplant to interpersonal coercion.

records.title: Educational and skills-based interventions for preventing relationship and dating violence in adolescents and young adults.
records.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
records.design: Cochrane systematic review PROTOCOL (intervention review, not yet completed synthesis)
records.population_setting: Adolescents and young adults, dating/relationship-violence prevention programmes
records.key_finding: Protocol only: states the objective is to evaluate benefits and harms of educational and skills-based interventions for preventing dating/relationship violence versus inactive controls; no outcome data reported yet.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (structurally): establishes that a Cochrane-standard systematic evaluation of exactly this intervention class (educational/skills-based recognition-type programmes) is underway/registered, which is useful to cite as the field's own gold-standard evidence bar T-PHE would eventually need to meet -- but it currently contains no findings, so cite as a protocol/registration only, never as supporting evidence of effect.

records.title: Can Attitudes Serve as Proxies for Behavioral Outcomes of Dating Violence Prevention Programs? Broader Lessons From a Pilot Evaluation of the Relationship Education Project.
records.design: Pre-post pilot evaluation, students in 19 middle/high schools, South Carolina
records.population_setting: US middle/high-school students, teen dating violence (TDV) prevention programme
records.key_finding: Favorable pre-post changes in attitudes toward controlling vs supportive dating behaviors were associated with lower incidence of some subsequent TDV behaviors, but the paper explicitly flags that attitude/knowledge change (the outcome type closest to 'recognition') has limited demonstrated correspondence to actual behavioral prevention across the wider literature.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates: directly relevant failure-criterion evidence -- this is exactly the caution T-PHE's Layer 0 claim needs to sit against: recognition/attitude-change outcomes are a weak, imperfect proxy for actual behavioral protection, so 'people recognised the pattern' cannot alone be equated with 'people were protected from manipulation'. Use to bound the awareness-protects claim, not to inflate it.

records.title: One-year follow-up of a coach-delivered dating violence prevention program: a cluster randomized controlled trial.
records.design: Cluster RCT, 16 high schools, N=1513 male athletes, 12-month follow-up
records.population_setting: US high-school male athletes (Grades 9-11), 'Coaching Boys Into Men' bystander-based dating-violence prevention
records.key_finding: In a 12-month follow-up of a cluster RCT (16 high schools, N=1513 male athletes), Coaching Boys Into Men (a coach-delivered dating violence prevention programme) showed NO significant 1-year effect on its primary recognition-of-abusive-behaviors outcome (-0.03, 95% CI=-0.15,0.09), intentions to intervene, gender-equitable attitudes, or positive bystander behaviors (0.04, 95% CI=-0.11,0.19). It DID show significant reductions in dating violence perpetration (-0.15, 95% CI=-0.27,-0.03) and in negative bystander behaviors i.e. laughing along with peers' abusive behaviors (-0.41, 95% CI=-0.72,-0.10).
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates: a directly on-point cluster-RCT dissociation between recognition and behavior -- this trial's primary 'recognition of abusive behaviors' outcome, the closest published analogue to T-PHE's Layer 0 mechanism, showed NO measurable 1-year improvement, even though a downstream behavioral outcome (perpetration) did improve via other programme components. This is strong caution against assuming 'improved recognition' is either necessary or the active ingredient behind any behavioral protection a programme like Layer 0 might eventually show -- recognition and protective behavior change appear here as separable, not automatically coupled, outcomes.

records.title: A cluster-randomized trial of a middle school gender violence prevention program: Design, rationale, and sample characteristics.
records.design: Cluster RCT design/protocol paper, 41 middle schools (38 clusters), N=973 male athletes ages 11-14
records.population_setting: US middle-school male athletes, adolescent relationship abuse/sexual violence prevention
records.key_finding: Design paper for a coach-delivered programme teaching recognition of harmful vs respectful relationship behaviors, gender-equitable attitudes, and positive bystander intervention; primary outcome is increase in positive bystander behaviors, measured at baseline, end of season, and 1-year follow-up.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (methodology template): useful as a template for how a recognition-of-harmful-behavior educational component is embedded and rigorously trial-designed (cluster randomization, multi-timepoint follow-up) in an adjacent adolescent population; no outcome data in this record (design paper only).
records.evidence_level: Cluster RCT protocol/design paper (no outcomes reported)

records.title: [Supporting the applicability and transferability of the "Sortir Ensemble & Se Respecter" program in France].
records.design: Implementation-science analysis using ASTAIRE tool and FIC (key functions, implementation, context) framework
records.population_setting: France; adaptation of the US 'Safe Dates' programme (via Swiss adaptation 'Sortir Ensemble & Se Respecter') for IPV prevention among young people
records.key_finding: Analyzes the applicability/potential transferability of a Safe-Dates-derived IPV prevention programme to a new (French) cultural context, describing its intervention theory and key functional 'ingredients' that must be preserved for the programme to work when transplanted across cultures.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (transferability caution): directly relevant to T-PHE's own cross-cultural transplant question (a Western-designed recognition/prevention programme model applied in a Thai context) -- shows the field explicitly treats cross-cultural transfer of a dating-violence-prevention programme as requiring formal adaptability analysis, not simple copy-paste; a methodological caution T-PHE's Layer 0 design should anticipate.

records.title: The Bystander Approach to Sexual Assault Risk Reduction: Effects on Risk Recognition, Perceived Self-Efficacy, and Protective Behavior.
records.design: Quasi-experimental treatment vs no-intervention control, N=103 undergraduate women
records.population_setting: US undergraduate women, sexual-assault-awareness/bystander-focused programme ('The Women's Program')
records.key_finding: Programme participants (vs control) reported greater ability to recognize risk cues, greater willingness to engage in self-protective behavior, following a single-session risk-recognition-focused intervention.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports: coercion/risk-recognition as a measurable, single-session-modifiable outcome in a comparable at-risk population -- structurally analogous to what a Layer 0 self-check/signals module aims to produce (improved recognition + intention toward self-protective behavior), though outcome here is self-reported perception/intention, not verified behavior change.

records.title: "Counteract the gaslighting" - a thematic analysis of open-ended responses about what women survivors of intimate partner sexual violence need from services.
records.design: Qualitative thematic analysis of open-ended survey responses, subsample from a cross-sectional survey
records.population_setting: Women survivors of intimate partner sexual violence (IPSV) who disclosed and sought help
records.key_finding: Survivors' own words identify that services need to actively 'counteract the gaslighting' they experienced -- i.e., help restore the survivor's own capacity to trust their perception of what happened -- as a named, felt need after disclosure; IPSV was described as often invisible/silenced in existing service responses.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (naming the mechanism): first-person qualitative evidence that survivors themselves frame gaslighting/perception-erosion as a distinct, nameable harm mechanism, and that having it explicitly counteracted/recognized is a stated need -- lends real-world texture to why Layer 0's 'recognise the pattern' framing may matter to the people it targets. Not evidence T-PHE's specific self-check delivers this.

records.title: Being silenced, loneliness and being heard: understanding pathways to intimate partner violence & abuse in young adults. a mixed-methods study.
records.design: Mixed-methods: qualitative interviews + Life History Calendars (17 women, ages 19-25) plus quantitative regression on ALSPAC longitudinal cohort (2127 female, 1145 male participants)
records.population_setting: UK young adults (ALSPAC birth cohort)
records.key_finding: Qualitative pathways to intimate partner violence and abuse (IPVA) centred on themes of being silenced and unheard; quantitative arm modelled associations between earlier childhood factors (e.g., maltreatment) and later IPVA experience in a large longitudinal cohort.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (population-level pathway context): situates recognition/voice as one node in a larger pathway toward IPVA vulnerability in young adults, i.e. awareness/being-heard is embedded in a wider causal web (childhood factors, social context) -- useful to avoid T-PHE overclaiming that awareness alone is sufficient; awareness is one lever among several upstream/downstream factors.
records.evidence_level: Mixed-methods, includes large longitudinal cohort component (ALSPAC)

records.title: Disclosure and Help-Seeking Experiences of Sexual and Gender Minority Victims of Intimate Partner Violence: A Mixed-Methods Study.
records.design: Mixed-methods, semi-structured interviews with N=41 SGM-AFAB young adults who experienced physical, sexual, or severe psychological IPV
records.population_setting: US sexual and gender minority young adults assigned female at birth
records.key_finding: Three-quarters of participants disclosed their IPV experience to someone; disclosure/help-seeking rates and helpfulness of responses varied by demographic subgroup and relationship to the person disclosed to, revealing structural and social barriers specific to this population.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (angle c, help-seeking after recognition): directly evidences that even after IPV is experienced, disclosure/help-seeking is not automatic and depends on population-specific barriers -- relevant to T-PHE's implicit assumption that recognition leads onward to protective action; recognition (labelling something as abuse) is necessary but the abstract does not establish it is sufficient for help-seeking.

records.title: Further psychometric examination of the Intimate Partner Violence Internalized Stigma Scale (IPVIS; Brunton & Harris, 2023): Examining criterion-related validity.
records.design: Psychometric/instrument-validation study
records.population_setting: IPV-victimized individuals (scale-validation sample)
records.key_finding: Provides further criterion-related validity evidence for the IPVIS, a scale measuring IPV self-stigma (awareness of and internalized agreement with negative IPV stereotypes), which the paper explicitly frames as a barrier to help-seeking, distinct from recognition of the abuse itself.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates: a caution/failure-criterion node -- even where recognition of coercive/abusive dynamics occurs, internalized stigma about being a 'victim' is a separately measured construct that can itself block help-seeking; T-PHE's Layer 0 (recognition) does not by itself address this downstream stigma barrier, so 'recognised the pattern' is necessary but not sufficient evidence of protection or of an unblocked path to support.

records.title: Generic Health Literacy Measurements for Adults: A Scoping Review.
records.journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
records.design: Scoping review, 19 identified generic health literacy measurement instruments
records.population_setting: Adults, generic (non-disease-specific) health literacy instruments across the literature
records.key_finding: Identifies 19 generic health literacy measures; most apply a multidimensional definition centred on individuals' abilities to access, appraise, understand, and apply health information and services, with Nutbeam's conceptual model and Sørensen's integrated model as the two most widely used theoretical foundations.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (angle d, health-literacy model): confirms the 'access -> understand -> appraise -> apply' (Sørensen) and Nutbeam multidimensional health-literacy frameworks are the field's established theoretical scaffolding, which T-PHE's Layer 0 self-check/signal-recognition design can be explicitly mapped onto (recognition = the appraise stage) rather than inventing a bespoke construct; general health literacy, not relationship-safety-specific.

records.title: Development of health literacy assessment tool for 9-10 Years old children in Thailand.
records.design: Instrument development: EFA + CFA, N=1650 Thai schoolchildren aged 9-10
records.population_setting: Thailand, primary-school-age children
records.key_finding: Developed and psychometrically validated a health literacy assessment tool for Thai children aged 9-10: starting from a 50-item pool, EFA identified a 4-dimension solution (access, understand, appraise, apply) explaining 36.05% of variance; CFA confirmed good model fit (GFI=0.937, CFI=0.903, RMSEA=0.040), and the abstract's own conclusion reports the final validated tool as 31 items (Cronbach's alpha=0.902), though the four subscale item counts given in RESULTS sum to 32 -- a minor internal inconsistency in the source abstract itself, not resolvable without the full text.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (angle e, Thai evidence base): directly Thailand-based methodological precedent showing that rigorous, locally-validated health-literacy instrument development (item pool, expert review, large-N field test, EFA/CFA) is achievable and already done in this exact country -- a template T-PHE's own self-check instrument could/should follow for psychometric rigor, though this instrument is general child health literacy, not relationship-coercion recognition specifically.

records.title: One Size Doesn't Fit All: Dating Abuse Against Women From the Perspective of South Asian Muslim Youth in Canada.
records.design: Exploratory qualitative study, N=11 South Asian Muslim participants
records.population_setting: South Asian Muslim youth, Canada (diaspora)
records.key_finding: Participants identified four culturally distinct domains in which South Asian Muslim women may experience/understand dating abuse differently: exposure to parents/community, sexual-nature behaviors, controlling behaviors, and psychological/emotional/verbal abuse -- supporting an intersectionality perspective on how recognition of abuse is culturally shaped.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (angle e, Muslim-context evidence): directly relevant to T-PHE's target population framing -- shows recognition of psychological/controlling abuse is not culturally universal but is filtered through community/family exposure norms specific to South Asian Muslim contexts, meaning a generic (Western) 'signals' checklist may need cultural adaptation to be recognisable/legible to a Muslim-Thai audience. Small qualitative sample (N=11), not generalisable on its own.

records.title: Reflections on attitudes, experiences, and vulnerability of intimate partner violence among Southeast Asian college women living in United States.
records.design: Qualitative focus-group study, N=18 Southeast Asian college women, ages 18-34
records.population_setting: Southeast Asian diaspora college women in the United States
records.key_finding: Five themes emerged: recognition of IPV, perception of individual vulnerability to IPV, experience/responses to IPV, help-seeking and support system, and prevention strategies -- with cultural norms shown to shape both recognition of IPV and willingness to seek help.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (angle e, Southeast Asian evidence): closest population-adjacent PubMed record to T-PHE's own target demographic; explicitly names 'recognition of IPV' as its own distinct, separately-themed construct from help-seeking, and shows both are shaped by Southeast Asian cultural norms -- supports treating Layer 0 recognition and Layer-onward help-seeking as related but analytically separate outcome domains for T-PHE's programme theory. Small qualitative sample (N=18), US diaspora not Thailand-resident population.

gaps_noted: No PubMed-indexed record found that directly measures 'recognition of coercive control/gaslighting' via a validated psychometric instrument specifically among adolescents/young adults in a premarital-education context (searches for 'coercive control recognition scale' and 'gaslighting recognition education' returned 0 or near-0 direct hits; adjacent constructs like IPV internalized stigma (PMID 39536684) and gaslighting-as-felt-need (PMID 38336660) were the closest substitutes found).

No PubMed-indexed Thailand-resident (as opposed to diaspora) study on recognition of emotional/psychological abuse or coercive control was found; the two most population-relevant records (26289454, 26442989) are Canada/US-diaspora South/Southeast Asian Muslim and Southeast Asian samples, not Thailand-resident populations -- a genuine evidence gap for angle (e) as specified.

No PubMed-indexed study was found that directly tests whether recognising/labelling a relationship pattern as 'abuse' causally predicts subsequent help-seeking in a premarital or pre-relationship (as opposed to already-victimized) population -- the help-seeking records found (37882155, 38336660, 26442989) all study people who already experienced IPV, not people using an anonymous early-signal self-check before harm occurs, which is T-PHE's specific Layer 0 use-case.

No inoculation/prebunking study specifically targeting interpersonal romantic-relationship manipulation techniques (as opposed to misinformation/vaccine/election content) was found on PubMed -- this is the single largest evidentiary gap between the inoculation literature (angle a, strong direct RCT evidence) and T-PHE's actual claimed mechanism (recognising manipulation within a personal relationship), meaning the inoculation-theory support for T-PHE is necessarily by analogy across domains, not a direct transplant.

The one Cochrane systematic review record found (42535453) is a protocol only, with no synthesized outcome data yet published -- the definitive systematic evidence base for 'do educational/skills-based dating-violence-prevention interventions work' is therefore still pending in the indexed literature as of this search date.
limits_of_this_search: PubMed-only (no PsycINFO/Scopus/grey literature), English-language esearch terms only (may miss Thai-language PubMed-indexed records if any exist), 18 esearch queries run with retmax 10-15 each (not exhaustive of all possible phrasings), record selection was manual triage of esummary titles rather than a systematic double-screened process, and abstracts were read in full via efetch but full-text articles were not retrieved -- key_finding numbers are as stated in abstracts only, not verified against full-text methods/results sections. No record in this set was independently interpreted as demonstrating that T-PHE itself is effective; T-PHE remains an untested programme theory and every 'supports' label above refers to analogous/adjacent mechanisms in other populations or domains, not to any evaluation of T-PHE.
